description: Test your knowledge of General Features, Joints, radiographs & surface marking (Lower Limb).

cards.text: What type of joint is the ankle, and what are its articular surfaces?
cards.answer: A synovial hinge joint. Articular surfaces: mortise (formed by tibial plafond, medial malleolus, lateral malleolus) and tenon (superior trochlea of talus).

tip.tip: Mortise-tenon = dovetail joint; visualize the talus fitting snugly into the ankle socket

cards.text: Name the 4 parts of the medial (deltoid) ligament and what it resists.
cards.answer: Anterior tibiotalar, posterior tibiotalar, tibiocalcaneal, and tibionavicular ligaments; resists excessive eversion. So strong it often causes medial malleolus avulsion fractures instead of tearing.

tip.tip: DELTA = Deltoid (4-part fan shape). Strength = avulsion not rupture

cards.text: Which lateral ankle ligament is most commonly torn, and in what mechanism?
cards.answer: Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) is most commonly torn in inversion + plantarflexion ankle sprains.

tip.tip: ATFL = Always Torn First in Lateral ankle sprains (inversion injury)

cards.text: Why is the subtalar joint important for inversion/eversion, and what is the clinical consequence of subtalar fusion?
cards.answer: Inversion and eversion occur at the subtalar joint, NOT the ankle joint. Subtalar fusion eliminates these movements, resulting in a stiff foot that struggles on uneven ground.

cards.text: What is the transverse tarsal (Chopart's) joint, and why is Chopart amputation clinically significant?
cards.answer: Midtarsal joint combining talonavicular (medial, ball-and-socket) and calcaneocuboid (lateral, saddle) joints; allows forefoot adduction/abduction. Chopart amputation preserves the hindfoot with tendon attachments for propulsion.

tip.tip: Chopart = functional forefoot preservation; preserves push-off power

cards.text: What is the iliotibial (IT) band, and what clinical problem does it cause?
cards.answer: Lateral thickening of fascia lata running from iliac tubercle to Gerdy's tubercle on tibia. Maintains knee extension and resists valgus stress. IT band syndrome: friction over lateral femoral condyle causes lateral knee pain in runners.

tip.tip: IT band = Runner's nemesis; friction = pain on lateral knee

cards.text: Which ligament of the ankle carries only 10–15% of axial load but is critical for stability?
cards.answer: The fibula, which forms part of the ankle mortise. Despite carrying minimal load, it is essential for ankle stability via the lateral ligaments.

tip.tip: Fibula = 'little bone' (Latin) but mighty stabilizer; don't underestimate it

cards.text: What are the dermatomes of the lower limb thigh and leg?
cards.answer: L1: inguinal/groin; L2, L3: anterior and medial thigh; L4: medial leg and medial foot.
